newsitem.title: UK: Euro VGO rises despite US/Dutch cracker problems.
newsitem.headline: Euro VGO rises despite US/Dutch cracker problems.

text.p: European VGO markets were stronger on Friday on U.S. demand despite problems at a catalytic cracker at Shell's Pernis refinery that will push significant volumes of high sulphur VGO on to the market.

German buying of low sulphur has died away amid weak supply with purchasers holding off till second-half August in the hope that production problems at large U.S. cracking facilities will limit trans-atlantic shipping and leave barrels available in Europe.
But the shutdown at Tosco's Bayway refinery does not seem to have yet affected U.S. appetite for residual fuels.

And although Shell will be selling out between 25 and 45,000 tonnes of VGO during an extended and brought forward three-month maintenance shutdown of one of its two cat crackers in Rotterdam traders were confident the market could support the extra supplies.
"We do see healthy demand from the U.S., despite the cracker problems there," one trader said. "We don't think they will have any difficulties selling VGO at economic levels.
He pegged high sulphur VGO cargo values in the mid 120s or slightly higher.
